subject: Re: Suncrest prepay terms — anchored flexible ladder proposal
messages:
From: Alex Holt <alex.holt@suncrest.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing structure for 2yr prepay

Karthik —

Thanks for the call earlier. We dug through our usage and modeling and want to formalize a request for a two‑year prepay structure. Key context: we expect a start near 300k tokens/month (month 1–3) with a fairly linear ramp to ~1.2M tokens/month by month 18, plus predictable seasonal spikes in Q4. Our procurement asks:

- A 2‑year committed prepay with quarterly true‑ups (no punitive clawback)
- A laddered discount tied to committed volume thresholds (we want the discount to increase as committed volume hits bands)
- Option to split billing across FYs (50/50 or frontload 60/40) — finance needs this flexibility
- Clarity on overage rates and on reserved capacity (we need assurance on throughput SLA during spikes)

Can you put a concrete pricing / term sheet we can review? Also looping in Priya (procurement).

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Holt
Head of Platform Engineering
Suncrest Labs
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Holt <alex.holt@suncrest.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing structure for 2yr prepay

Alex —

Appreciate the usage breakdown — very helpful. Attached is a concise term sheet that reflects a pragmatic approach we’ve used for similar accounts (attached: Suncrest_Redwood_Prepay_Term_Sheet_v1.pdf). Highlights of the initial offer:

- Commitment: 24 months, prepay for committed tokens up front (flexible split accepted — we can do 60/40 or 50/50 invoicing per your preference)
- Pricing: base discount 15% off list for the committed volume; ladder bands at >= 1.0M/month equivalent add +4%, >=1.5M/month add +6% (stacking is capped at +8%)
- Frontload option: an additional 2% credit if you frontload >=60% of the two‑year value in year 1
- True‑up: quarterly true‑up at committed unit rate; overage billed at committed unit rate * 1.1 (10% premium) — no punitive backcharge after quarterly true‑up
- Reserved capacity & SLA: we’ll reserve dedicated burst capacity on Redwood Dedicated for Q4 spikes; SLA credit tiers are included in the term sheet
- Early termination: prorated refund of unconsumed prepay less administrative fee; early termination after month 12 requires 60 days notice

If you need a steeper discount for procurement, let me know the internal target and I’ll route an approval request. Vanessa / Irene — can you confirm whether finance can accept a 60/40 split (Y1/Y2) and whether the 2% frontload credit is acceptable from a margin perspective?

Next steps: Priya/Alex — feedback on bands and the split, and if you’re comfortable we’ll produce a DocuSign-ready term sheet.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Strategic Accounts (Americas)
Redwood Inference

Karthik —

Thanks for the quick send. A few follow ups from procurement: 

- Target discount: our CFO is looking for ~20–22% effective discount on committed spend to justify the cash outlay. Is there flexibility if we commit to a minimum ARR floor and put a PO across both years?
- True‑up cadence: monthly true‑ups would be preferable (easier forecasting) rather than quarterly — will that change overage treatment?
- Billing split: we prefer 50/50 billing across FYs; can you confirm the invoice schedule you’d support and whether that will be acceptably reflected in the DocuSign SOW?

We’re buyer‑sensitive to termination language — can you also provide a short example of the prorated refund calc so our legal team can review?

Priya

- Accepts monthly true‑ups with the agreed overage uplift (10%)

Irene — can you confirm the margin impact? Vanessa — if approved, I’ll send v2 of the term sheet with the adjusted bands and DocuSign link.

Karthik
